notes.action3d.boot: A step on the loading screen while the game builds its hall of stone.
notes.action3d.knight: The last wave's boss, an armoured knight: the note as it marches in, and its name over its health bar.
notes.action3d.hud.hp: Hit points: the label beside the hero's health bar. Keep it two or three letters.
notes.action3d.hud.wave: The top-left corner in play: the wave (as 3/5) and the score, with three spaces between them.
notes.action3d.hint.combo: A button prompt's word, after the key ("J combo"): the three-hit sword combo. The controls hint lists six such prompts in one row, so keep each word short.
notes.action3d.hint.dash: A button prompt's word, after the key: dash.
notes.action3d.hint.jump: A button prompt's word, after the key: jump.
notes.action3d.hint.bolt: A button prompt's word, after the key: throw an ember bolt (a magic fire shot).
notes.action3d.hint.lock: A button prompt's word, after the key: lock on to the nearest monster (Zelda's targeting).
notes.action3d.hint.camera: A button prompt's word, after the key: change the camera.
notes.action3d.over.won: The title over the end screen when all five waves are beaten.
notes.action3d.over.all_waves: The end screen after a win: {count} is the number of waves (5). Another stat follows on the same row.
notes.action3d.over.wave_of: The end screen after a loss: the wave the hero fell in, of how many.
notes.action3d.over.defeated: The end screen: how many monsters the hero defeated.

brief: The 3D action slice: a torch-lit hall where a lone swordsman fights five waves of monsters (husks, skeletons, slimes, wisps) and then a knight, like Zelda 64's dungeons or Diablo. The hero is a man and is never named; the words are an arcade-style HUD, short button prompts and an end screen, mostly in capitals.
